Obey Them That Have the Rule
oh-BAY them that hav thuh rool
phrase
From Hebrews 13:17; the charge to submit to the elders who oversee and watch for souls in the church.

📖 Biblical Definition

Obey them that have the rule over you is the charge of Hebrews concerning the believer’s duty to the elders who oversee the church: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you. The rule spoken of is not the lordship of a tyrant but the spiritual oversight of shepherds appointed by Christ to lead, feed, and guard the flock. The believer is to obey and submit—to receive their teaching of the Word, follow their godly leading, and yield to their oversight—not blindly, for their rule is under Christ and bounded by His Word, but readily and gladly, as to those who watch for his soul and must give account for it. The same chapter bids, Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow. This submission is the appointed order of Christ’s church, by which the flock is kept and fed; and it is for the believer’s own good, for elders who must labour in grief rather than joy is unprofitable for the very souls they serve. The dictionary honors this charge as the Scripture’s call to honour and submit to the godly oversight of elders—a submission under Christ and His Word, ready and joyful, for the good of the soul—against both the lawless individualism that submits to no one and the tyranny that lords it over God’s heritage.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Hebrews’ charge to obey and submit to the elders who oversee the church and watch for souls; a glad submission under Christ and His Word, for the good of the soul.

OBEY THEM THAT HAVE THE RULE, the charge to submit to the elders (Heb 13:17).

The rule is spiritual oversight, not the lordship of a tyrant.

Obey and submit, for they watch for your souls.

📖 Key Scripture

Heb 13:17 — "Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you."

Heb 13:7 — "Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation."

1Pe 5:5 — "Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble."

1Th 5:12 — "And we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The charge is twisted into authoritarian control, or rejected by lawless individualism; Scripture calls for glad submission to godly oversight under Christ and His Word.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition beyond two opposite errors. The first twists the charge into authoritarian control, where elders lord it over God’s heritage, demanding unquestioning obedience and binding the conscience where Scripture has left it free—the very abuse Peter forbids when he charges elders not to be lords over God’s heritage but ensamples to the flock. The second error is the lawless individualism that rejects all oversight, submitting to no one, treating the charge to obey them that have the rule as an intrusion on personal autonomy.

The principle to recover is glad submission to godly oversight, under Christ and His Word. The rule of elders is real but bounded: it is spiritual oversight, the leading of shepherds who have spoken unto you the word of God, whose faith you are to follow (Heb 13:7), not a tyranny that binds the conscience apart from Scripture. To such oversight the believer is to obey and submit (Heb 13:17), to know and esteem those who are over him in the Lord (1 Thess 5:12), clothed with the humility that submits (1 Pet 5:5). This submission is for his own good, for elders who must watch over souls in grief rather than joy is unprofitable for those souls. The order of Christ’s church is neither tyranny nor anarchy, but the glad, humble submission of the flock to the godly oversight of shepherds who watch for souls and must give account.
